before.title: Melting and Cracking Dashboard
before.description: Early-to-mid R35 dashboards use a soft-touch material that degrades under heat and UV. The dash pad melts to a shiny, reflective surface that throws glare onto the windshield, emits a chemical odor, and cracks/splits along the vent, gauge-cluster and console edges. It became the subject of a Florida class-action (Heuer v. Nissan North America, Case No. 0:17-cv-60018) alleging Nissan refused to cover replacements, and it is widely reported on GT-R owner forums.
before.solution: Replace the dashboard assembly (labor-intensive full dash-out job) or, more commonly among owners, wrap/recover the dash pad in Alcantara or suede to eliminate glare and cover cracks. Some owners use aftermarket dash covers as a low-cost interim fix.
symptoms: Dash surface becomes shiny/reflective and melts in heat
Glare on windshield from reflective dash
Cracks and splits at vents, cluster and console edges
Chemical/plastic odor in cabin on hot days

before.title: OEM Brembo Cross-Drilled Brake Rotor Cracking and Warping
before.description: The factory two-piece cross-drilled Brembo rotors crack around the drilled holes and warp under repeated hard or track use. The car's ~4,000 lb weight, heat concentration at the drill holes, and limited brake cooling cause stress cracks and thickness variation. Owners typically get only 2-3 track days from a set of factory rotors, and report high-speed braking shudder sometimes confused with pad-deposit judder.
before.solution: Replace rotors; for track/heavy use owners upgrade to curved-vane / high-carbon two-piece rotors (AP Racing, STILLEN, DBA, Alcon) with better pads, which last several times longer than the OEM cross-drilled discs. Proper pad bedding reduces deposit-related shudder.
symptoms: Braking shudder/pulsation at high speed
Visible cracks radiating from cross-drilled holes
Steering-wheel vibration under braking
Rapid rotor wear after track days

before.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Dead Battery When Parked
before.description: R35s (particularly CBA and DBA-generation cars, roughly 2008-2016) suffer parasitic battery drain when parked because the AV/audio unit fails to go to sleep with the ignition off and keeps sending an 'amplifier ON' signal, leaving the amp drawing current. BCM faults and hard-wired aftermarket accessories also contribute. Because these are low-mileage weekend cars that sit, owners frequently return to a dead 12V battery.
before.solution: Perform a parasitic-draw test to isolate the circuit; the common fix is a relay bypass for the amp or repair/replacement of the failing AV unit. Owners commonly diagnose by pulling the 15A AUDIO fuse in the battery-room fuse box overnight. Keep the car on a battery tender during storage.
symptoms: Dead 12V battery after the car sits days to weeks
Repeated jump-starts needed
Measurable current draw with ignition off
Battery going flat despite being relatively new

citations.title: Almost found the source of the parasitic battery drain! | GTRLife
Parasitic electrical drain on the battery | GTRLife

proposal.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Dead Battery When Parked
proposal.description: Exact GT-R communications describe AV-control-unit diagnosis, configuration and replacement procedures. They do not establish that the AV unit keeps the amplifier awake, that BCM faults recur across 2009-2016 or that pulling the 15-amp AUDIO fuse identifies the cause. Low-use storage, battery condition, accessories and module wake-up are separate contributors, and the frozen forum citations are not primary evidence.
proposal.solution: Fully charge and test the battery, allow every module to enter sleep mode, then measure key-off current without repeatedly waking the network. Isolate the circuit with service-manual procedures and inspect aftermarket wiring before replacing modules. Do not buy a battery, amplifier, AV unit, BCM, relay or battery tender from this page; measured draw, sleep timing, circuit and programming requirements must be established first.

key-off current measured after verified sleep time

before.title: Steering Knuckle / Rear Axle Housing Insufficient Strength (Recall 21V402000)
before.description: NHTSA recall 21V402000 (Nissan campaign R21A4) covers front steering knuckles and rear axle housings that received insufficient heat-treatment. A gap in a furnace door lowered the temperature in one zone, leaving affected parts with poor hardness. If the knuckle or axle housing takes a strong impact (e.g. a curb strike) it can deform, causing loss of steering control or, in severe cases, wheel separation. The campaign also covers certain 2020 Murano, INFINITI QX60/QX50/Q50 models.
before.solution: Under recall, dealers inspect and replace the affected front steering knuckle and rear axle housing free of charge. Owner notification letters went out July 26, 2021. Owners should verify their VIN against the recall.
symptoms: Off-center steering wheel after an impact
Wheel misalignment / uneven tire wear
Potential wheel separation in severe cases

before.title: TPMS Sensor Failure and RF Interference Faults
before.description: The R35's direct 315 MHz tire-pressure sensors are prone to faults, especially on early cars where the original sensor batteries are now well past their 7-10 year life, throwing 'no data' and sensor-fault codes (C1708/C1709/C1710/C1711). Nissan TSB NTB13-088A also documents that aftermarket electronics (phone chargers, dash cams) plugged into the 12V sockets can interfere with the signal and trip false TPMS warnings.
before.solution: Replace dead/failed sensors and program the sensor IDs to the ECU with the correct tool (professional installation, or a tuning tool such as Cobb/EcuTek plus a TPMS activation tool). For interference-related faults, remove or relocate the offending aftermarket electronics per the TSB.
symptoms: Persistent TPMS warning light
'No data' or sensor-fault messages
Intermittent warnings when charging a phone / running a dash cam
One or more tires not reporting pressure

before.title: Transmission Bellhousing Bearing Failure and Rattle
before.description: The R35's rear-mounted GR6 transaxle connects to the front-mounted VR38DETT via a driveshaft inside a cast-aluminum bellhousing. Because there is no torque tube, the engine/bellhousing move independently of the transmission, creating constant push/pull loading that wears the bellhousing support bearing until it wallows out the soft aluminum housing and the shaft floats freely. It presents first as a metallic rattle from the front of the car on/off throttle. This is a distinct, well-documented failure from GR6 clutch judder because it is the engine-to-driveshaft support, not the dual-clutch pack.
before.solution: Replace the worn bearing and, because the aluminum housing is usually already damaged, install an upgraded billet/reinforced bellhousing (e.g. ATR-style with hardened steel insert sleeve and upgraded Japanese bearings) rather than another OEM unit. Requires dropping the driveshaft and often the transmission.
symptoms: Metallic rattle from front of car on acceleration/deceleration
Vibration through driveline under load
Noise that quiets when clutch/driveline is unloaded
Rattle worsens over time as bearing float increases

before.title: GR6 Dual-Clutch Transmission Judder and Failure
before.description: The Nissan GT-R GR6 dual-clutch transmission (built by BorgWarner) develops judder during low-speed maneuvers, parking, and first gear takeoffs. The clutch packs wear unevenly, and the transmission control module software can cause harsh engagement. Track use accelerates wear dramatically. before.title: Turbo Oil Feed Line Leak (VR38DETT Engine)
before.description: The GT-R VR38DETT twin-turbo engine can develop oil leaks from the turbocharger oil feed and return lines. The banjo bolt sealing washers degrade over time, causing oil to drip onto the hot exhaust components - a potential fire hazard. This is more common on 2009-2016 models and after high-boost tuning.
before.solution: Replace turbo oil feed and return line sealing washers with new copper crush washers. Inspect oil lines for cracking. Some owners upgrade to braided stainless steel oil lines. Cost: $200-800 at a GT-R specialist. Critical to address immediately due to fire risk.
symptoms: Oil smell from engine bay
Visible oil on turbo housings
Smoke from engine bay after hard driving
Oil dripping on exhaust
Low oil level between changes

before.title: Twin Turbo Wastegate Rattle at Idle
before.description: The VR38DETT's twin turbocharger wastegate actuators develop a characteristic rattle or flutter at idle and light throttle. The wastegate flapper valves vibrate in the exhaust stream, creating a metallic buzzing sound. While not performance-affecting in most cases, the rattle worsens over time and can indicate wastegate actuator diaphragm wear that eventually causes boost control issues.
before.solution: Mild wastegate rattle is common and not harmful. If the rattle is excessive or accompanied by boost fluctuation, the wastegate actuators need adjustment or replacement. An actuator rebuild kit ($100-$200 per side) is available for DIY. Aftermarket external wastegate conversions ($1,500-$3,000) eliminate the problem entirely for heavily modified cars. Stock cars should have the actuator rod adjusted at the dealer.
symptoms: Metallic buzzing or rattling at idle
Flutter sound on light throttle tip-in
Rattle increases with engine age
Occasional boost spike or fluctuation
Sound comes from rear/center of engine bay

proposal.description: The frozen page cites Nissan NTB12-045 as a GT-R turbocharger wastegate-rattle bulletin, but that reference is for 2011-2012 Juke rear-seat rattle. No matching GT-R wastegate communication appears in the exact 197-row corpus. The frozen page does not support a 2009-2024 actuator-diaphragm wear population, boost-control progression, dealer rod adjustment or universal external-wastegate conversion.
proposal.solution: Localize the metallic noise with the engine cold and warm, record boost deviation and DTCs and inspect heat shields, exhaust hardware, turbo linkage and actuator command before adjustment. Do not alter a wastegate rod without the exact service specification. Do not buy an actuator, rebuild kit, turbocharger or external-wastegate conversion from this page; noise source, boost-control fault and exact turbo fitment must be established first.
